title: Exercise in Nature Improves Performance and Mood
paragraphs: A run through the forest might do more than put you in a good mood. A new study suggests it could help you run farther without feeling like you're working harder — and leave you wanting to do it again.

To test this, researchers in the UK and Switzerland asked 47 healthy adults aged between 18 and 31 to do two 30-minute runs: one in an urban area and one in a forest. The participants were asked to run at a pace that felt comfortable but "somewhat hard."

The researchers recorded how far participants ran and monitored their heart rates during each run. Afterward, participants answered questions about how hard the run felt, how much they enjoyed it, their mood and whether they would like to run again in the same location.

The results showed that participants ran significantly farther in the forest than they did in the city, even though they felt they were putting in the same effort. There was no significant difference in their average heart rates between the two runs.

The participants' enjoyment, mood and intention to run again were also significantly higher after a run in the forest. Participants were not only more likely to say they would like to run again in the forest in the near future, they were also more likely to say they would do it regularly over the next 12 months.
One of the study authors, Matthew Putland, said, "The message is simple: the easiest and cheapest way to improve exercise habits and enjoyment is to do it in nature."
